title: Accessing 100 GHz Mechanical Modes in Bulk Crystals at Cryogenic Temperatures
authors: Boxuan Tian, Jiacheng Xie, Hong X. Tang
abstract: Sub-terahertz electromechanics offers a promising route to probe mechanical quantum motion at experimentally friendly Kelvin temperatures. Traditionally, high-frequency mechanical resonators rely on advanced microfabrication to shape complex microstructures, while bulk crystals have been largely overlooked due to their large inertia and challenging transduction at such frequencies. Here we show that bulk lithium niobate can host mechanically accessible modes near 100 GHz when coupled via plug-and-play three-dimensional microwave cavities. This approach enables efficient, non-contact excitation of centimeter-scale, milligram-mass vibrational modes across 7.0--110 GHz, with mechanical quality factors up to 30,000 at W band. Furthermore, using a frequency-tunable superconducting niobium cavity at 4 K, we demonstrate strong coupling between a microwave cavity mode and multiple mechanical modes, enabling coherent energy exchange between microwave photons and mechanical phonons with cooperativity up to 16.6 at 110 GHz. These results establish a versatile platform for accessing massive high-frequency mechanical modes and for precision tests of mechanical quantum physics at elevated temperatures.
summary: The authors developed a novel method to study mechanical quantum motion in bulk crystals by coupling them non-contactly into superconducting microwave cavities. They achieved high quality factors for vibrational modes near 100 GHz at cryogenic temperatures. This platform enables the observation of strong, coherent energy exchange between microwave photons and mechanical phonons, advancing macroscopic quantum physics experiments.
main_problem: The research aims to access and study mechanical quantum motion at high frequencies (near 100 GHz) using bulk crystals while maintaining low dissipation.
main_result: They successfully demonstrated strong coupling between microwave cavity photons and multiple mechanical phonon modes in a bulk lithium niobate platform, achieving high quality factors up to 30,000.
method: The study uses superconducting niobium cavities coupled non-contactly to bulk crystals (LiNbO3) and characterizes the system using microwave spectroscopy (S11 measurements) at cryogenic temperatures.
model_or_system: The platform is a piezoelectric cavity–phonon system utilizing bulk lithium niobate. The interaction is modeled by an effective Hamiltonian describing coupling between cavity photons ($\hat{a}$) and mechanical phonons ($\hat{b}$), leading to the observation of avoided crossings in the spectrum.
key_observables: Mechanical quality factors ($Q_b$) up to 30,000; Cooperativity ($C$) up to 16.6; Measured spectral shifts and linewidths via S11 fitting.
important_parameters: Operating frequencies near 100 GHz; Cryogenic temperatures (4 K); Effective vibrational masses in the milligram range.
main_assumptions: The use of non-contact coupling minimizes surface losses, and analysis relies on fitting complex S11 spectra to cavity-phonon models.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, measured S11 spectra at room and cryogenic temperatures showing mechanical resonances, and avoided crossings confirming strong coupling between microwave photons and phonons.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the feasibility of non-contact coupling in bulk LN to characterizing high-$Q$ mechanical modes across a wide frequency band, culminating in demonstrations of coherent energy exchange (strong coupling) at cryogenic temperatures.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental realization of a high-frequency quantum transducer platform, directly testing cavity QED concepts (photon-phonon coupling) using macroscopic mechanical oscillators, which is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum transducers.
